headline: A Russian court fined a woman about $178 after her AI-made photo of a bear on a village street, sent to a friend as a joke, spread and sent rangers out searching.
score_reason: Quirky and clear, but local in scale; the same story is also C16-10 from Reuters.
importance_line: It shows that fake AI images can set off real searches and fines, in a country already frightened by deadly bear attacks; it is a small court fine.
summary: Reuters reports, in a story carried by India Today and citing a statement from the Amur courts' press service, that a court in Russia's Far East fined a woman 15,000 roubles after she used ChatGPT to make an image of a brown bear walking down a street in Magdagachi and sent it to a friend as a joke. The picture spread, residents called the police and the district head sent wildlife rangers to look for a bear that did not exist; a similar case in the Transbaikal region earlier brought a 30,000-rouble fine, while real bear attacks have killed at least 26 people since spring, according to the news agency RIA Novosti.
